edits.purpose: State scalar applicability and finite-coordinate Euclidean remainder aggregation
edits.source_excerpt: [F4] Taylor's formula with bounded derivatives controls the remainders uniformly on a compact convex tube. [[thm-multivariable-taylor-formula-with-lagrange-remainder]]
edits.proposed_replacement: [F4] The cited Taylor theorem is scalar. A compact convex tube $K\Subset U$ has an open convex neighborhood contained in $U$, so the theorem can be applied separately to each scalar coordinate function on the stipulated segments; it can also be applied to each scalar coordinate of a trajectory on its local time interval. Intermediate points may depend on the coordinate. If the coordinate remainders satisfy $|R_i|\le C_i r^s$, their vector satisfies $\|R\|_2\le(\sum_i C_i^2)^{1/2}r^s$. [[thm-multivariable-taylor-formula-with-lagrange-remainder]]

edits.purpose: Derive the O(|h|) displacement from the fixed-point equation and prove both vector Taylor remainders coordinate by coordinate
edits.source_excerpt: 1.4 The fixed-point equation and [F4] give $Z=z+(h/2)F(z)+(h^2/4)DF(z)F(z)+O(|h|^3)$ uniformly on the tube: first $Z-z=O(|h|)$ by the ball bound, then Taylor-expand $F(Z)$ at $z$ and substitute once. Consequently $2Z-z=z+hF(z)+(h^2/2)DF(z)F(z)+O(|h|^3)$. The exact flow has the same expansion by [F3], [F4], and [F6], so its one-step defect is at most $C|h|^3$. [A1, F3, F4, F6, given]
edits.proposed_replacement: 1.4 Put $m=2d$ and $\delta=Z-z$. The admitted fixed-point equation gives $\|\delta\|\le |h|\|F(Z)\|/2\le |h|M/2$, hence $\delta=O(|h|)$ uniformly. Since $H\in C^3$, $F\in C^2$. Apply the scalar theorem [F4] to each $F_i$ along $[z,Z]$: $F_i(z+\delta)=F_i(z)+DF_i(z)\delta+R_i$, where $R_i=\tfrac12D^2F_i(z+\vartheta_i\delta)[\delta,\delta]$ for some $\vartheta_i\in(0,1)$. These points may differ with $i$. Bounded second derivatives on the tube give $|R_i|\le C_i\|\delta\|^2$, hence $\|R\|_2\le(\sum_{i=1}^m C_i^2)^{1/2}\|\delta\|^2$. Substitution into $\delta=(h/2)F(z+\delta)$ first gives $\delta=(h/2)F(z)+O(h^2)$ and then $\delta=(h/2)F(z)+(h^2/4)DF(z)F(z)+O(|h|^3)$. Thus $2Z-z=z+hF(z)+(h^2/2)DF(z)F(z)+O(|h|^3)$. For the exact flow, write $g_i(t)=(\varphi_t(z))_i$. By [F3] and [F6], $g_i^{(1)}=F_i(\varphi_t(z))$, $g_i^{(2)}=DF_i(\varphi_t(z))F(\varphi_t(z))$, and $g_i^{(3)}=D^2F_i(\varphi_t(z))[F(\varphi_t(z)),F(\varphi_t(z))]+DF_i(\varphi_t(z))DF(\varphi_t(z))F(\varphi_t(z))$ are defined, with the third derivative uniformly bounded on the controlled trajectories. Scalar Taylor in time gives $g_i(h)=z_i+hF_i(z)+(h^2/2)(DF(z)F(z))_i+(h^3/6)g_i^{(3)}(\eta_i h)$ for $h\ne0$, with possibly distinct $\eta_i\in(0,1)$. Each last term is bounded by $C_i'|h|^3$; summing their squares gives a Euclidean remainder bound $(\sum_{i=1}^m(C_i')^2)^{1/2}|h|^3$. The case $h=0$ is immediate. The exact flow therefore has the same terms through degree two as $2Z-z$, giving the uniform one-step defect $C|h|^3$ for either sign of $h$. No common Lagrange intermediate point for the vector is used. [A1, F3, F4, F6, given, algebra]

actual_scalar_supplier_and_coordinate_re.inspected: Full current Statement, Facts & Assumptions and Proof; scalar C^(k+1) function on an open convex domain, reduced to one-variable Taylor along a segment.
actual_scalar_supplier_and_coordinate_re.field_expansion: Apply k=1 to each C2 scalar F_i. Distinct vartheta_i are permitted; coordinate remainder bounds C_i||delta||^2 imply a vector bound sqrt(sum C_i^2)||delta||^2.
actual_scalar_supplier_and_coordinate_re.flow_expansion: The C2 field gives C3 scalar trajectory coordinates by differentiating the ODE. Apply scalar k=2 Taylor in time to each g_i, allowing distinct eta_i; bounded third derivatives give a vector O(|h|^3) bound by summing squares.
actual_scalar_supplier_and_coordinate_re.displacement: The fixed-point equation and admitted F bound give ||Z-z||<=|h|M/2. A fixed radius alone is not used to infer O(|h|).
actual_scalar_supplier_and_coordinate_re.domain: An open epsilon-neighborhood of compact convex K is convex and can be chosen inside U; all evaluated segments/trajectories lie in the stipulated controlled tube.
